item.title: Let's Walk!! Brookdale Park — Sat Sep 12, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! If entering from Bellevue Avenue and park in the first parking lot on the left. We will be gathering near the the playground area.
if entering from Watchung Ave, park and walk up to the upper parking lot near the playground area.
We will be walking the outer path. There are several break-off points if you do not want to walk the entire path.
The walk will be about an hour or at least 3-4 miles.
Wear comfortable shoes!
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.
Brookdale Park offers the public access to both passive and active recreational activities as well as picturesque vistas. Trails for walking and running, lush groves and extensive lawns, playgrounds, sports fields, track facilities, tennis courts, an archery range and stadium grandstand are just some of the numerous attractions that make Brookdale Park a magnet for nature lovers, families, and physical fitness enthusiasts for miles around.
https://www.essexcountyparks.org/parks/brookd

item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Tue Sep 15, 7:00 PM
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series — Mon Oct 5, 5:30 PM — Cole Hall 141
item.description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14. This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. Mondays, beginning September 145:30–7:30 p.m.Cole Hall, Room 14110-week series We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us. Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at calarotaa@montclair.edu
Hosted by: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence

Did you love silent reading time in school? Are you more of an introvert that loves books, but doesn't want to jump into a discussion group? Are you looking to read more, but struggle to sit down and just DO IT? If you answered 'yes' to any of these, you might like Silent Book Club! Each month, we meet around Montclair and enjoy each other's company with a book of our own choosing.

There is also "Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Monday Morning". If you are interested, please register here
If you prefer to play the game on the weekend, please register for the "Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Saturday Afternoon" by clicking here
If you're new to the game, and would like to teach yourself at your own pace, please register for the "Teach Yourself Mah Jongg" by clicking here.
